claims.assertion: Mari says past events shape present identity, so she favors accepting good and bad experiences and learning from them.
claims.speaker: Mari Swaruu

claims.assertion: In her model, changing an event through time travel creates an alternate timeline; it does not alter the traveler’s remembered origin line.
claims.speaker: Mari Swaruu
claims.qualifiers: This is the Taygetan time-travel model she describes.

claims.assertion: She says decisions create timeline branches, events occur once within each line, and paradoxes therefore cannot form.
claims.speaker: Mari Swaruu

claims.assertion: She considers imagined-past revision a limited but potentially useful coping tool, with effectiveness varying by person.
claims.speaker: Mari Swaruu

coverage_gaps: Her personal account of childhood events and alternate timelines
